subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard read/write/exec deny boundary for that skill directory, or should OpenClaw keep it as prompt eligibility state and add a separate strict skill-access policy?
rationale: Both paths are plausible, but this changes public security semantics and can affect existing trusted workflows, so automation should not choose the permanent boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Make disabled skills a hard boundary
options.body: Treat `enabled:false` as deny-by-default for prompt exposure, file reads/writes, exec/sandbox access, Gateway status, docs, and tests, with migration notes for trusted workflows.

options.title: Add separate strict skill-access policy
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` as prompt eligibility only and introduce an explicit operator-controlled policy for skill directory filesystem and exec denial.

options.title: Document trusted-filesystem semantics only
options.body: Close the security expectation gap in docs while telling multi-user deployments to use workspace/sandbox/exec policy controls instead of skill toggles.

recommendation.title: Make disabled skills a hard boundary
recommendation.body: Treat `enabled:false` as deny-by-default for prompt exposure, file reads/writes, exec/sandbox access, Gateway status, docs, and tests, with migration notes for trusted workflows.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and security/skill hardening history make steipete the best available routing owner for the product/security boundary decision.
